topic: The one-page resume that gets shortlisted for your first internship: copy this structure, section by section
save_reason: A one-page resume format, section by section, shown as a real resume screen: 'copy this structure'. The full section-by-section format is in the caption as copyable text.
send_reason: Send this to a friend applying this month.

cover.concept: Studio still life on flat saturated orange: one crisp sheet of paper standing upright in a brass bulldog clip, crumpled sheets scattered around it.
hooks: The one-page resume for your first internship. (ambition, owner-approved)
Put projects above skills on your resume. (curiosity)
You can finish this resume in one evening. (confidence)
This is a strong second-year resume. (awe)
cover.hook: The one-page resume for your first internship.
cover.lineDraft: Copy this one page in your first year.

slides.label: Save this
slides.idea: Results first + save promise: the whole one-page resume, 5 sections top to bottom.
slides.title: This is what a strong first resume looks like.
slides.line: Save its 5 sections for your first application.
slides.screen: A whole one-page resume (fictional Aarav Sharma) shown small with its 5 sections boxed and named: Header, Education, Projects, Skills, Achievements

slides.label: Section 1
slides.idea: Put your links at the top: name, email, phone, GitHub, LinkedIn, portfolio.
slides.title: Put all your links at the top.
slides.line: Email, phone, GitHub, LinkedIn and portfolio go in one line.
slides.screen: Resume header cropped big: Aarav Sharma, aarav@example.com, +91 98xxx xxxxx, github.com/aarav-codes, linkedin.com/in/aarav-example, aarav.example.com

slides.label: Section 2
slides.idea: Projects come before skills: 2-3 projects, what it does, the tech, a live link.
slides.title: Put your projects above your skills list.
slides.line: Recruiters look for what you built, with a live link.
slides.screen: Resume Projects section cropped big: 'Bus Timings | React, Node | live link' with two bullets, then a second project

slides.label: Section 3
slides.idea: Write each bullet as what you built and what it does: 'Built X using Y so users can Z'.
slides.title: It's not the tasks or the tools you list.
slides.line: It's what you built and what it does for users.
slides.device: not A or B, it's C
slides.screen: Two resume bullets compared: a weak one 'Worked on a website' struck in red, and a strong one 'Built a bus-times app with React and Node so students can check live bus times' marked green (fictional)

slides.label: Before you send
slides.idea: Print it and read it out loud once; you catch typos and long lines.
slides.title: Here's a quick check: read it out loud once.
slides.line: You'll catch typos and lines that run too long.

slides.label: Screenshot this
slides.idea: Cheat sheet: one page; links on top; education; projects before skills; skills; achievements; bullets = action + result; save as firstname-lastname-resume.pdf.
slides.title: This won't work unless it fits on one page.
slides.line: Screenshot this checklist and tick it before you send.
slides.screen: A Google Docs page titled 'Resume checklist' with 6 ticked lines (.row.on): One page, Links on top, Projects before skills, Action + result bullets, Hackathons and clubs last, PDF named aarav-sharma-resume.pdf
